title: Automotive hex bolt
description: a steel hex head bolt, item number 90017-RJA-0030, used as a high-strength automotive fastener
reference_excerpt: The product in question is a steel hex head bolt, specifically described as an indented hex flange head fastener with a fully threaded shaft, intended for use in automotive applications. The classification process began by considering the proposed HTS code 7318.15.2065; however, it was determined that the item does not meet the criteria for a bolt as it can be turned during assembly and does not necessarily require a nut for its intended function. Instead, it is classified as a screw based on the supplementary criteria of ASME B18.2.1.

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 7318 covers screws, bolts, nuts and similar threaded articles of iron or steel; no chapter/section note excludes bolts used in vehicles as parts because Section XVI note (f) exclusion applies to articles of Section XVI/XVII only when principally used as parts of machines classified there, but standard fasteners like bolts remain classified in 7318 per heading text and chapter note practice

classification.rationale: The item is a finished steel hex-head bolt used as a fastener, which is classified under heading 7318 (screws, bolts, nuts and similar threaded articles of iron or steel) per GRI 1; Section XV/XVI notes do not remove ordinary fasteners from this heading merely because of automotive end-use. At the 6- and 8-digit level it falls in 'other screws and bolts' with shank/thread diameter of 6 mm or more (7318.15.80), and at the statistical suffix level, being a non-stainless hex-head bolt that is not a cap, set, or socket screw, it falls in 'With hexagonal heads: Other: Other' (7318.15.80.69), consistent with prior CROSS rulings (e.g., H86188) on carbon-steel hex bolts used in engine/automotive applications, though the exact diameter was not confirmed.
